sentences.text:
This Criminal Petition, under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. (New Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023), is filed by the petitioners/A.2 and A.3 seeking anticipatory bail in connection with Crime No.275 of 2024 of Ibrahimpatnam Police Station, NTR District, registered Matta Venkateswara Rao vs The Station House Officer on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123657046/
1 for the offences punishable under Sections 495, 417, 420 and 120B read with 34 I.P.C.
2.

entities.text: Matta Venkateswara Rao vs The Station House Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard Sri V.Hemanth Kumar, the learned counsel for petitioners and the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent-State.

3. Perused the record.
4.
In Crime No.275 of 2024 there are three accused.
A.1 is a woman and she was arrested and was remanded to judicial custody on 17.07.2024.
The investigation is in progress.

The present petitioners are A.2 and A.3 and they are the parents of A.1.
5.
The de facto complainant in this case is the husband of A.1 and thus, son-in-law to A.2 and A.3/the present petitioners.

The allegations are that the present petitioners solemnized the marriage of their daughter/A.1 with the de facto complainant on 05.09.2018 and during their wedlock a girl child was born to them on 06.07.2019.
The above mentioned dates are crucial.
The allegations are that before solemnization of marriage of A.1 with the de facto complainant, she was already married to Sri Pusapati Vijaya Raju on 31.08.2007.
She had filed F.C.O.P.No.1406 of 2018 before the learned Judge-Family Court-cum-V Additional District Judge, Visakhapatnam.

entities.text: Judge-Family Court-cum-V Additional District Judge, Visakhapatnam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: By that petition she sought divorce from her husband Sri Pusapati Vijaya Raju.
On 08.10.2020 an ex parte decree of divorce was passed by the learned Family Court.
Thus, the marriage of A.1 was subsisting till the said final decree dated 08.10.2020.
While so, her marriage with de facto complainant was solemnized on 05.09.2018.

The allegations are that these petitioners being parents of A.1 had full knowledge of the facts of the subsisting marriage of their daughter/A.1 and concealing the same fraudulently they performed the marriage of their daughter with the de facto complainant.

At paragraph No.3 of the present bail petition, the petitioners have mentioned that:
"3. It is respectfully submitted that the de facto complainant, knowing fully well about the fact that the spouse of the accused No.1 is very much alive, has married the accused No.1 out of the love developed between them and the petitioners being the parents have performed the marriage."
This contention of the petitioners substantiates the essence of the allegation made by the prosecution.

6. A reading of the F.I.R. does disclose that the married lady/A.1 had earlier filed Section 498-A I.P.C. case as against her first husband and she had also filed another Section 498-A I.P.C. case as against her second husband.
Both of them are pending.

7. It is in the context of the above facts, the contentions of the petitioners seeking anticipatory bail are that they are old and sick and have permanent residence.
8.

Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor strongly opposed the petition stating that in the name of marriage this crime has been perpetuated and the innocents have been put to task on the ground of matrimonial harassments.
